ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A $2\mathrm{kg}$ object is placed on a horizontal ground and pulled horizontally by a light spring with an original length of $8\mathrm{cm}$. When the object just starts to move, the length of the spring is $11\mathrm{cm}$. When the spring pulls the object at a constant velocity, the length of the spring is $10.5\mathrm{cm}$. The spring constant is known to be $200\mathrm{N/m}$, and $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{=} 10\mathrm{N/kg}$.

1. What is the maximum static friction force acting on the object?
2. What is the magnitude of the sliding friction force acting on the object?
3. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the ground?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A $2\mathrm{kg}$ object is placed on a horizontal ground and pulled horizontally by a light spring with an original length of $8\mathrm{cm}$. When the object just starts to move, the length of the spring is $11\mathrm{cm}$. When the spring pulls the object at a constant velocity, the length of the spring is $10.5\mathrm{cm}$. The spring constant is known to be $200\mathrm{N/m}$, and $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{=} 10\mathrm{N/kg}$. 1. What is the maximum static friction force acting on the object? 2. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a block placed on a horizontal ground, with a horizontally placed spring connected on the right side. The spring is pulled to the right, so the pulling force is along the horizontal direction and has no vertical component; the supporting force of the ground on the object and gravity are balanced in the vertical direction. Reasoning calculation: It is known that the original length of the spring is l0=8 cm, the spring stiffness coefficient is k=200 N/m, the object mass is m=2 kg, and g=10 N/kg. 1. When the object is just about to start moving, the spring length is 11 cm, and the elongation Δx=11 cm-8 cm=3 cm=0.03 m. The spring pulling force F=kΔx=200×0.03=6 N. When it is just about to move, the spring pulling force is equal to the maximum static friction force, so the maximum static friction force is 6 N. 2. When the object moves at uniform speed, the spring length is 10.5 cm, and the elongation Δx=10.5 cm-8 cm=2.5 cm=0.025 m. The spring pulling force F=kΔx=200×0.025=5 N. Uniform motion indicates that the resultant force in the horizontal direction is zero, so the magnitude of the sliding friction force is equal to the spring pulling force, which is 5 N. 3. Since the pulling force is horizontal, the vertical supporting force N=mg=2×10=20 N. The kinetic friction coefficient μk=fk/N=5/20=0.25.
